newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles warns ruling may hurt development.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles warns ruling may hurt development.

text.p: The Community Redevelopment Agency (CRA) of Los Angeles said on Thursday that a court ruling could scuttle plans for new bonds for projects but does not put holders of outstanding debt at risk.
On Wednesday, the 2nd District Court of Appeal in Los Angeles shot down the city's plan to lift the redevelopment agency's $750 million spending cap.

In its ruling, the appeals court affirmed the judgment of the trial court, which held in 1995 that it lacked jurisdiction to modify the cap or debt limit for the so-called Central Business District Redevelopment Project.
Attorneys who opposed the city's plan to lift the cap said Wednesday's ruling could scuttle billions of dollars of future bond issues by the agency.

The CRA said its future bonding plans could not be quantified, but added that the ruling, unless overturned, would prevent it from issuing bonds for its Central Business District project in downtown Los Angeles.
"Without being able to lift that cap we will not have the funds we need," said Dov Lesel, an assistant Los Angeles city attorney who also serves as general counsel to the CRA.
"We would have been doing bonding, we would have been able to jump start work," Lesel said. "But all of it requires money. This (plan) has pretty much been foreclosed."

The CRA said the appeals court ruling would have no impact on the agency's outstanding bonds because it has been placing a portion of its tax revenues in an escrow account as a security measure. "There's no risk of default," Lesel said.
Lesel said the CRA would review its legal options, but he added that he was "leaning toward" filing an appeal to California's Supreme Court.
